introduction: The project's steering directives gain a version and a dated record of their amendments, carried in YAML frontmatter the directives themselves never see. Every phase still receives the directives, now with the version named and the record withheld. A package records in its PRD frontmatter the version it was generated against, and the verdict names, for a draft or active package written under an earlier version, the amendments made since. Nothing is refused because of it: a package that has fallen behind is reported, and a person who has checked it clears the warning by changing the field.

glossary.MAJOR bump: An amendment that raised the first number of the version, which by the documented meaning marks a directive removed, or changed so that a package or code that followed it may now break it.
glossary.amendment: One entry of the steering's record: a version in the version form, a date in YYYY-MM-DD and a non-empty sentence saying what changed. The entries are newest first, their versions strictly decreasing and their dates not increasing, and the first entry's version is the file's version.
glossary.steering_malformed: The warning a command raises for a steering file whose frontmatter breaks one or more of the well-formedness rules. It is high, it names every rule broken, and it never changes a command's exit code.
glossary.steering_version: Both the optional PRD frontmatter field that records which steering version a package was generated against, and the name of the verdict rule that compares that field with the spec root's steering.
glossary.the version form: Three non-negative integers separated by full stops, with no leading zeros and nothing after the third: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Two versions in this form are compared as three integers, never as text.
glossary.versioned: Said of a steering file that opens with well-formed frontmatter and whose body says something. Such a file has a version a package can record. A file with no frontmatter, one whose frontmatter breaks a rule, and one whose body says nothing are all unversioned.

requirements.title: Reading the steering's version and its record
requirements.rationale: A version nothing can read is a comment; the reader is what turns the record into something the verdict and the prompts can use.

criteria.condition: steering.md opens with a YAML frontmatter block delimited by lines of three hyphens
criteria.action: read the version and the amendments from that block, and take everything after the closing delimiter as the body
criteria.contract: the body a caller receives holds none of the frontmatter's bytes; the version is the frontmatter's version; the amendments are its list in file order, newest first

criteria.condition: steering.md does not open with a frontmatter block
criteria.action: take the whole file as the body, report no version and no amendment, and raise no warning
criteria.contract: the body is the file's bytes as they are, the steering is unversioned, no warning is raised, and every caller behaves as it does today

criteria.action: for any steering file, treat its frontmatter as well-formed exactly when it holds only the keys version and amendments, its version is in the version form, it holds at least one amendment, every amendment has a version in that form, a date in YYYY-MM-DD and a non-empty change, the amendment versions strictly decrease, the amendment dates do not increase, and the first amendment's version is the file's version
criteria.contract: a file meeting every rule is versioned and raises no warning; a file breaking any one of them is malformed, as 16-REQ-2.1 says. The rules are checked in the order they are listed above, and a rule whose subject an earlier broken rule has already rejected is not checked: an absent version breaks only "the version is in the version form", and an amendment with no version breaks only "every amendment has a version in that form", so one fault is one named rule

criteria.action: for any two versions in the version form, compare them as three integers rather than as text
criteria.contract: 2.10.0 is newer than 2.9.0, 1.0.1 is newer than 1.0.0, 2.0.0 is newer than 1.99.99, and 1.0.0 equals 1.0.0

criteria.condition: a steering file's body, taken after the frontmatter, is empty, is only the placeholder marker, is only the bare heading, or is over the 24 KB bound
criteria.action: report the file as nothing: no body, no version and no amendment
criteria.contract: the body is the empty string and the steering is unversioned, so a package written against it records no version; the bound is measured over the body alone, so a file whose body is within it and whose frontmatter pushes the whole file over is read as it would be without the frontmatter

requirements.title: A steering file whose frontmatter breaks a rule
requirements.rationale: A record nobody checks drifts into fiction, and a run that stopped because of a mistyped date would make the record cost more than it is worth.

criteria.condition: a steering file's frontmatter breaks one or more of the well-formedness rules
criteria.action: report every rule it breaks, return the body all the same, and report the version as absent
criteria.contract: the reader names each broken rule, one per rule, in a fixed order; the body is what follows the closing delimiter; the steering is unversioned, so nothing records a version against it

criteria.condition: a steering file opens with a frontmatter delimiter that is never closed
criteria.action: report it as malformed, take the whole file as the body, and report the version as absent
criteria.contract: one broken rule is named, saying the frontmatter has no closing delimiter; the body is the file's bytes as they are; the steering is unversioned

criteria.condition: spec runs against a spec root whose steering file is malformed
criteria.action: raise one high steering_malformed warning naming every broken rule, before the first model call, and run every phase as it would otherwise
criteria.contract: exactly one warning with code steering_malformed and severity high, at stage preflight, whose message names each broken rule; the exit code is the one the run would have had; every phase is given the body

criteria.condition: speca <package> --validate runs against a spec root whose steering file is malformed
criteria.action: raise the same warning once and give the verdict it would otherwise give
criteria.contract: exactly one high steering_malformed warning at stage preflight; exit code 0; result.valid and every entry of result.validation are what they are under an unversioned steering

requirements.title: What every phase is given
requirements.rationale: A phase needs the directives and the version they carry; the history of how they got there is cost without use.

criteria.condition: a phase's prompt is built and the spec root's steering is versioned
criteria.action: put the body in the steering block and name the version in it
criteria.contract: the block holds the line "Steering version <version>" before the body, and the text between the BEGIN STEERING and END STEERING markers holds none of the frontmatter's bytes

criteria.condition: a phase's prompt is built and the steering is unversioned or malformed
criteria.action: build the steering block as it is built today, with no version line
criteria.contract: the block is byte-identical to the one built from the same directive text before this change

criteria.action: for any steering file and any phase, keep the amendment record out of the prompt
criteria.contract: no amendment's date and no amendment's change text appears anywhere in the prompt, for every phase that is given the steering: the split decision, the three artifact phases, the architecture phase and the PRD review

criteria.condition: the steering has nothing to say, by 16-REQ-1.5 or because the file is missing, a symlink or unreadable
criteria.action: put no steering block in the prompt
criteria.contract: the prompt holds no "## Steering" heading, no BEGIN STEERING marker and no version line, as today

requirements.title: The package's record of the version
requirements.rationale: The verdict can only name the amendments a package missed if the package says which version it was written under.

criteria.action: for any package, carry an optional steering_version in the PRD frontmatter and round-trip it through a save and a load
criteria.contract: a package whose prd.md holds steering_version loads with that value, and a save writes the same key with the same value, after schema_version and before owner; a package without it loads without it and a save writes no such key; both still validate

criteria.condition: spec writes a package and the spec root's steering is versioned
criteria.action: write the steering's version into that package's prd.md
criteria.contract: the written prd.md holds steering_version with the steering's version, for every package a split writes, and each package still validates

criteria.condition: spec writes a package and the steering is unversioned, is malformed or has nothing to say
criteria.action: leave the field out of the package it writes
criteria.contract: the written prd.md holds no steering_version key at all, rather than an empty or null one

criteria.condition: a prd.md holds a steering_version that is not in the version form
criteria.action: report it as a schema error on prd.md
criteria.contract: one error with check json_schema and artifact prd.md whose path names steering_version; result.valid is false

criteria.condition: the steering_version of an active package is changed in its prd.md and the package is saved
criteria.action: accept the write and leave the intent hash as it was
criteria.contract: the save returns no error, the intent_hash in prd.md is unchanged, no intent drift is reported, and the package still validates

requirements.title: The steering_version rule in the verdict
requirements.rationale: Someone has to be told which amendments a package was not written under, and the verdict is where a person already looks.

criteria.condition: the verdict is taken on a draft or active package whose steering_version equals the spec root's steering version
criteria.action: report nothing under the rule steering_version
criteria.contract: no entry with check "steering_version" is in the verdict's errors or warnings

criteria.condition: the verdict is taken on a draft or active package whose steering_version is older than the spec root's steering version
criteria.action: report one warning under the rule steering_version naming both versions and every amendment made after the package's version
criteria.contract: one warning with check "steering_version" and artifact "prd.md", whose message holds the package's version, the steering's version, and for each amendment newer than the package's, newest first, its version, its date and its change

criteria.condition: the verdict is taken on a draft or active package whose steering_version is older than the spec root's
criteria.guard: one of the amendments made since raised the MAJOR number
criteria.action: say in that same warning that a directive the package was written under has been removed or changed
criteria.contract: the one warning of 16-REQ-5.2 also carries that sentence, and no second entry under the rule is reported

criteria.condition: the verdict is taken on a draft or active package whose steering_version is newer than the spec root's, or names a version the amendment record does not hold
criteria.action: report one warning under the rule steering_version that says which of the two it is
criteria.contract: one warning with check "steering_version" and artifact "prd.md", naming the package's version and the steering's, and saying either that the package's version is newer than the steering's or that it is in no amendment of the record

criteria.action: for any package that is sealed, superseded or archived, for any package with no steering_version, and under a steering that is unversioned or malformed, report nothing under the rule steering_version
criteria.contract: no entry with check "steering_version" is reported, whatever the two versions are

criteria.action: for any package, report every finding of the rule steering_version as a warning and never as an error
criteria.contract: no error with check "steering_version" is ever reported, so the rule never makes result.valid false and never refuses an activation

execution_paths.title: A maintainer amends the steering and the verdict names what a package missed

steps.action: adds a directive to steering.md and a new amendment at the top of the record, raising the MINOR number
runs speca <package> --validate on an active package written under the earlier version
reads the spec root's steering, compares the two versions, and reports one warning under the rule steering_version naming both and the amendment made since
reads the package against that amendment, finds it still holds, and changes steering_version in its prd.md to the new version
takes the verdict again and reports no finding under the rule, the versions now being equal

execution_paths.title: A run records in the package the steering version it was generated against

steps.action: runs spec on an input against a spec root whose steering is versioned
reads the steering once, and gives every phase the body with the version named and the amendment record withheld
writes the package with steering_version set to the steering's version
validates what it wrote and reports no finding under the rule steering_version, the versions being equal
reads the written prd.md and finds the steering version the package was generated against

execution_paths.title: A run against a malformed record warns once and uses the directives all the same

steps.action: mistypes a version in the amendment record, so that the amendment versions no longer strictly decrease
runs spec on an input against that spec root
raises one high steering_malformed warning at preflight, naming the broken rule, before the first model call
gives every phase the directives all the same, with no version named
writes the package with no steering_version, the version being absent, and the run ends with the exit code it would have had
